statements.text: This is a national security issue. We will not compete with China. We are at an arms race in artificial intelligence with China, and we don't have the mineral production, the mining, the processing, the refining to be competitive.
statements.context: Verbatim transcript of a congressional hearing titled 'Powering America's Future: Unleashing American Energy,' where Mr. Palmer warns about US competitiveness in AI against China.

statements.text: Would you agree that we are in a technology arms race with China for dominance in AI and quantum computing? [...] the bottom line is is that it is going to require enormous amounts of power [...] they are really focused on hydrocarbon coal-based power generation. [...] and this is the existential threat to the United States. It is also a threat to our economy. [...] I think ensuring that we maximize our access to high energy density [...] is not just an economic issue. It is a national security issue [...]
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on U.S. energy reliability, where Rep. Gary Palmer questions witnesses on the energy implications of the AI competition with China.

statements.text: My concern too is we are in an arms race for artificial intelligence. And I am looking at the NERC report on the high-risk areas and the medium-risk areas, and it is clear we don't have the power capacity to build the data systems that we need in order to win that arms race with China.
statements.context: Remarks at a House Energy Subcommittee hearing on electricity demand and reliability.

statements.text: We are in an arms race with China for artificial intelligence and quantum computing. What amount of power generation, in addition to what we have now, will we need?
statements.context: Remarks delivered at a policy event titled 'America's AI Moonshot: The Economics of AI, Data Centers, and Power Consumption.'

statements.text: If we lose the arms race in artificial intelligence and quantum computing to China, they will be the superpower, not a superpower. [...] One of the things that I think we need to be taking a look at in addition to the power generation is our dependence on China for critical minerals and rare earth elements.
statements.context: Verbatim remarks by Mr. Palmer during a hearing on AI economics, data centers, and power consumption.

statements.text: What do you consider a greater threat to our future national security, losing the AI arms race to China or climate change?
statements.context: Question posed by a lawmaker to a witness at a hearing on AI economics, data centers, and power consumption.

statements.text: My concern is that we are in an arms race with China for artificial intelligence and quantum computing, and that if China wins that race they will not be a superpower, they will be the superpower.
statements.context: House hearing on AI technology, human discovery, and American global competitiveness.

statements.text: considering that we are in an arms race for artificial intelligence with China, should not we be looking at rather than investing in more renewables, investing in nuclear or maybe more hydrocarbon, power generation so that we will have the ability to power the data centers that we are going to need to compete in AI.
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled 'Mandates, Meddling, and Mismanagement: The IRA's Threat to Energy and Medicine,' where a member questions a witness on energy policy and AI competitiveness.

statements.text: We are also seeing a lot of unwanted and scam robotexts, and AI generated phone calls and text messages, including voice clones and deepfakes. [...] In August, the FCC proposed rules to protect consumers from AI-generated robocalls and robotexts.
statements.context: Congressional subcommittee hearing opening statement on illegal robocalls and robotexts, chaired by Rep. Gary Palmer.

statements.text: In August, the FCC proposed rules to protect consumers from AI-generated robocalls and robotexts. These are steps in the right direction, and I applaud the coordination we have seen thus far.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Palmer at a House Energy & Commerce subcommittee hearing on illegal robocalls and robotexts.

statements.text: We are in an arms race for artificial intelligence and quantum computing with China. And in order to meet that, we are going to have to have some permitting reform.
statements.context: Opening statement at a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on the Environment hearing on Clean Air Act permitting reform.

statements.text: this race for artificial intelligence is for one thing only, and that is to determine who will be the superpower. Whoever wins this race will not be a superpower; they will be the superpower. [...] So one of my main objectives right now is to get this critical infrastructure built [...] so that we can decouple ourselves from China in that regard. It is absolutely a top national security issue.
statements.context: House committee hearing on brownfields reuse legislation, where Representative Palmer pivots to AI competition with China and the infrastructure needed to support it.
